html:
The Duchy of Savoy was a state in the western Alps ruled by the House of Savoy, made a duchy in 1416. It is on the map for 1530 and 1600.

It straddled the mountains, with Savoy proper on the French side and Piedmont on the Italian side, and it controlled key Alpine passes. That made it valuable and vulnerable. In 1536 France occupied most of it, and Geneva broke away to become the city of John Calvin.

Duke Emmanuel Philibert won it back. He commanded the Spanish army that beat the French at Saint-Quentin in 1557, and the peace of 1559 returned his lands. In 1563 he moved the capital from Chambéry to Turin, turning the state toward Italy. His successors kept playing France and Spain against each other. In 1720 the dukes became kings of Sardinia; see Sardinia-Piedmont. That kingdom later united Italy.
sum: The Duchy of Savoy was a state in the western Alps ruled by the House of Savoy, made a duchy in 1416. It is on the map for 1530 and 1600.
